subject.title: fix(wechat): preserve existing accounts across hot reload

question: Must this provider-backed WeChat lifecycle fix show redacted live account-A/account-B QR-login evidence before merge, or may the focused gateway regressions and normal CI satisfy the proof threshold?
rationale: The remaining gap is not a mechanical code repair: the contributor has repeatedly and accurately stated that their environment cannot run the real WeChat session, while the branch changes user-visible account availability during reload.

options.title: Require live WeChat proof
options.body: Keep the PR blocked until someone with a real QR-login setup attaches redacted evidence that account A remains online after account B is added.

options.title: Accept gateway-level proof
options.body: Explicitly waive provider-level proof and allow the lifecycle regressions plus exact-head CI to be the merge evidence for this narrowly scoped gateway change.

recommendation.title: Require live WeChat proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR blocked until someone with a real QR-login setup attaches redacted evidence that account A remains online after account B is added.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline identifies joshavant as a gateway review contact; no stronger owner signal was available from the provided review evidence.
